_note: The expected verdict for the committed M0 spike-4 fixture set. This run was a deliberately non-compliant script, so `fail` and exit 2 are correct. If a change makes this file wrong, read the fixture before editing the file: the fixture is the measurement.
_finding_codes_are_review_queue_codes: `finding_codes` names codes that appear in `Verdict::review_queue`, which holds Flag and Fail findings only. A Pass-level code (`goal_recovered`, `join_key_agrees`, `normalisation_applied`, `no_version_drift`, `token_summary`, `stripped`) is a statement the verdict makes and never a queue entry, so none is listed here. The list is compared for SET EQUALITY: a code listed that the run does not raise, and a code raised that is not listed, both fail.
_v8_is_pass_here: The two tool-id spaces match exactly on this fixture, so V8 reports `join_key_agrees` alone and its verdict is `pass`.
_v10_no_longer_reports_the_manifest: V10's old flag for a store declaring no `partition_key` left this list on 2026-09-04. It read the CONNECTOR MANIFEST rather than the trace, so it said the same thing on every run of this connector; `ConnectorManifest::validate()` now refuses a store that declares neither a `partition_key` nor an `unpartitioned_reason`, and claude-code-cli's `main` and `raw_bodies` carry the reason. V10 raises `foreign_records_present` here, which is about these bytes rather than about the manifest — and since 2026-09-05 it says so at Pass, so V10's verdict is `pass` (see the task-13 note below).
_v9_is_flag_here: An M0 capture predates the daemon and carries no event stream, so V9 raises `no_event_stream` (Flag) on all three fixtures: store-rewrite and config-deviation reconciliation are unverifiable here, which is not the same as clean.
_v13_is_pass_here: V13 (the trace is bound to a server-signed start and closes at the run's deadline) joined on 2026-09-04. This descriptor declares `[[leg1]]` stores and no `chain`, so it predates the daemon's start receipt and carries none to check: V13 is `pass` with exactly one finding, `legacy_trace`. That finding is Pass-level and therefore never a review-queue entry, so `finding_codes` below is unchanged — no `receipt_missing`, no `seal_not_chained`, and no other V13 code. A `connector_dir_unbound` Flag joined this list on 2026-09-06 and left again in fix round 1, which is why the file returns to the shape it had: every statement V13 makes about the connector DIRECTORY is read out of a receipt whose signature verified, and a capture with no receipt has no such document to be old. `legacy_trace` already says no start was carried, and a second Flag beside it reported the same absence twice.
_parser_census_is_a_statement_not_a_find: `parser_census` is the record kinds the parser recognised and deliberately ignored, counted (`ParsedLegs::census`). A statement, never a finding: nothing here enters `finding_codes` or moves `overall`. It is in this file because the alternative is silence — 48 of `main` + `subagent`'s 148 records are dropped, in 9 kinds, and two of them (`last-prompt`, `queue-operation`) carry the human's text verbatim. SCOPED to the entry's own stores: the descriptor's third store, `a9-other-folder`, is the `foreign = true` A9 probe and drops 7 more (`queue-operation` 2, `atis-latch` 3, `last-prompt` 2) that belong to V10's story and are absent here. That scoping is what makes the total 48 rather than 55.

_nine_findings_became_pass_level_on_2026: Task 13. Nine informational findings fired at Flag on every honest trace, which put them in `review_queue` and made `Severity::Pass` unreachable for a run that broke no rule. They are now Pass-level: every sentence still appears in `Verdict::checks`, and none appears in the queue. Four left this file's `finding_codes`: `cross_leg_identifiers` (V3, the tool-id counts), `resume` (V4, the transcript's one resume marker), `model_changed` (V5, the four models the script switched between) and `user_slot_excluded` (V6, three harness-authored records the catalogue kept out of the user slot); `foreign_records_present` (V10, the A9 probe declared foreign) left it too. Three check verdicts moved with them — V5, V6 and V10 are now `pass` — and V3 and V4 stay `flag` because each still raises a code of its own: `leg2_without_leg1_record` on V3, `second_root_thread` and `foreign_session` on V4. Nothing about these bytes changed; what changed is which half of the verdict says so.
_cause_excluded_message_witnessed_by_fie: m2/verifier-cut removed the V3 excluded-twin join (`excluded_twin`/`exclusion_rule`) and the human-rule exclusion catalogue's application, so `excluded_message_witnessed_by_field` no longer exists. Leg-2 post 16, the `<task-notification>`, is again reported as plain `leg2_without_leg1_record` — its leg-1 twin (`main` seq 56) is still excluded, now via the ordinary positive test (`origin.kind` is not `human`) rather than the deleted catalogue, but nothing rejoins the two any more. V6 also stops naming this record by its old catalogue id: all four harness-authored records here now group under one `user_slot_excluded` finding labelled `failed_positive_test`.
